interactions.label: A patient with progressive unilateral sensorineural hearing loss shows worsening

params.question: A patient with progressive unilateral sensorineural hearing loss shows worsening speech discrimination at higher sound intensities, an absent stapedial reflex, and prolonged wave V on auditory brainstem response. This triad localises the lesion to which level?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Middle ear pathology produces conductive hearing loss with an air-bone gap on audiometry — not sensorineural hearing loss with rollover.

In cochlear disease, speech discrimination holds steady at high sound intensities. The rollover phenomenon — worsening discrimination at higher levels — distinguishes retrocochlear from cochlear pathology.
Correct. Rollover, absent stapedial reflex, and prolonged ABR wave V together localise the lesion to the retrocochlear pathway, raising strong suspicion for an acoustic neuroma.
Central auditory processing disorders present differently — typically with bilateral involvement and difficulty processing competing signals, not this specific triad.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the retrocochlear localisation triad: rollover (worsening speech discrimination at higher intensities), absent stapedial reflex, and prolonged ABR wave V. In cochlear disease, discrimination holds steady — rollover is the distinguishing sign.
Well done. The retrocochlear triad — rollover, absent stapedial reflex, and prolonged ABR wave V — is the key bedside combination that raises suspicion for a cerebellopontine angle tumour.

interactions.label: Noise-induced hearing loss showing a bilateral symmetric 4 kHz audiometric notch

params.question: Noise-induced hearing loss showing a bilateral symmetric 4 kHz audiometric notch can be reversed with early high-dose corticosteroid therapy.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Noise-induced hearing loss is irreversible. The bilateral 4 kHz notch reflects permanent cochlear hair cell destruction that no treatment can reverse. You may be confusing it with sudden sensorineural hearing loss, where high-dose corticosteroids within the first week offer the best chance of recovery. The key contrast: sudden SNHL is urgent and treatable; noise-induced hearing loss is preventable but never reversible.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Noise-induced hearing loss is permanent and irreversible — damaged cochlear hair cells do not regenerate. High-dose corticosteroids are the time-sensitive treatment for sudden sensorineural hearing loss, an entirely different condition. Prevention through hearing protection at 85 dB or above is the only strategy for noise-induced loss.

interactions.label: A 55-year-old patient reports a whooshing sound in the left ear that beats in ti

params.question: A 55-year-old patient reports a whooshing sound in the left ear that beats in time with the heartbeat. Which investigation is most appropriate?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While audiometry provides a baseline, pulsatile tinnitus synchronous with the heartbeat signals a vascular cause. Audiometry alone cannot exclude a glomus tumour or arteriovenous malformation.

answers.text: MRI with gadolinium of the internal auditory canal

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: MRI with gadolinium is indicated for unilateral non-pulsatile tinnitus to exclude acoustic neuroma. Pulsatile tinnitus requires vascular imaging — MR or CT angiography — to identify the source.
Correct. Pulsatile tinnitus beating with the heartbeat signals a vascular aetiology — glomus tumour, arteriovenous malformation, or carotid stenosis. Vascular imaging is the mandatory investigation.
Electrocochleography evaluates endolymphatic hydrops in suspected Meniere's disease. It has no role in the workup of pulsatile tinnitus.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the two tinnitus rules: pulsatile = vascular imaging (MR or CT angiography); unilateral non-pulsatile = MRI with gadolinium to exclude acoustic neuroma — even if the audiogram is normal.
Well done. The rule is straightforward: pulsatile tinnitus means vascular imaging. Unilateral non-pulsatile tinnitus means MRI. Hold both triggers.

interactions.label: A patient reports recurrent episodes of spinning lasting two hours, accompanied

params.question: A patient reports recurrent episodes of spinning lasting two hours, accompanied by fluctuating low-frequency hearing loss and low-pitched roaring tinnitus. Which additional feature completes the diagnostic tetrad of Meniere's disease?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A positive Dix-Hallpike test confirms benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, in which vertigo lasts seconds — not the hours-long episodes seen in Meniere's disease.
Ear discharge suggests middle ear infection. In Meniere's disease the tympanic membrane appears normal; the pathology is endolymphatic hydrops, not infection.
Correct. Aural fullness — a sensation of pressure in the affected ear — is the fourth component of the Meniere's tetrad and the most commonly omitted feature on examinations.
Facial nerve palsy is not part of Meniere's disease. Its presence alongside hearing loss and vertigo should prompt investigation for a cerebellopontine angle tumour.

overallFeedback.feedback: The Meniere's tetrad: (1) episodic vertigo lasting 20 minutes to hours, (2) low-frequency fluctuating sensorineural hearing loss, (3) low-pitched roaring tinnitus, and (4) aural fullness. Aural fullness is the most frequently forgotten component.

Well done. The full Meniere's tetrad: episodic vertigo (20 minutes to hours), low-frequency fluctuating SNHL, low-pitched roaring tinnitus, and aural fullness. Missing the fourth feature is the commonest exam error.

interactions.label: The 1-3-6 rule mandates hearing aid fitting by six months of age. What is the pr

params.question: The 1-3-6 rule mandates hearing aid fitting by six months of age. What is the primary reason for this urgency?

answers.text: The cochlea is structurally immature before six months

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The cochlea is structurally complete at birth. The urgency relates to central auditory development — specifically auditory cortex plasticity — not peripheral organ maturation.

answers.text: Otoacoustic emissions are unreliable before six months

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: OAE testing is performed as early as the first month of life — it is the recommended newborn screening tool in the 1-3-6 rule.

answers.text: The auditory cortex is most plastic in the first two years of life

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Early amplification during the critical period of auditory cortex plasticity enables age-appropriate language development. A child implanted before 12–18 months can develop normal language; identified at age four, that child faces lifelong deficits.

answers.text: Connexin 26 mutations only become detectable after six months

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Connexin 26 is a genetic cause of congenital deafness present from birth and detectable by genetic testing at any age. The 1-3-6 timeline is driven by neural plasticity, not mutation detectability.

overallFeedback.feedback: The urgency of the 1-3-6 rule stems from auditory cortex plasticity, which peaks in the first two years. A child fitted with hearing aids by six months can develop age-appropriate language; one identified at four years faces lifelong language deficits.
Well done. The 1-3-6 rule is a race against the closing window of auditory cortex plasticity — screen by one month, confirm by three, intervene by six.
